intervals.label: operating, first CEvNS observation
intervals.note: Start is a lower bound only: no fetched source states the exact installation date, and the detector could not have taken the data behind the August 2017 observation before the September 2015 proposal. Recorded as approximate/uncertain 2015 rather than left unbounded; end is bounded above by the fact that the CsI full-dataset paper (arXiv:2110.07730, submitted 2021-10-14) already describes the detector as decommissioned by then.
intervals.quote: We observe this process at a 6.7-sigma confidence level, using a low-background, 14.6-kg CsI[Na] scintillator exposed to the neutrino emissions from the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

intervals.label: decommissioned
intervals.note: No fetched source states an exact decommissioning date; 2021 is used only as an upper bound because the full-dataset paper (submitted 2021-10-14) already describes the detector as decommissioned. Recorded as approximate/uncertain rather than left unbounded.
intervals.quote: New data collected before detector decommissioning have more than doubled the dataset since the first observation of CEvNS

placements.note: Exact deployment and decommissioning dates are not sourced; see the intervals.
placements.quote: CEvNS was first observed ... 19.3 m from the neutrino source using a 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillating detector

summary.plain: A 14.6-kilogram crystal of caesium iodide that made the first direct observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, a process predicted for decades but never before caught.
summary.technical: 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillating crystal, low-background configuration, deployed in Neutrino Alley at the SNS; produced the 2017 first observation of CEvNS (6.7σ) and the 2022 cross-section measurement from the full dataset before decommissioning.
